title: Normalized principal-quotient cone augmentation on K-flat sheaf complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R,S$ sheaves of commutative rings, and $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring-sheaf map. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction $\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and unbounded cochain localization $Q_R$ with cone convention $C(f)^q=Y^q\oplus X^{q+1}$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(dy+f(x),-dx)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $r$ be a global section of $R$ with $\varphi(r)=0$, and assume the sequence of $R$-module sheaves
$$0\longrightarrow R\xrightarrow{r}R\xrightarrow{\varphi}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi S\longrightarrow0$$
is exact. For every K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], put $C_r(P)=C(r\operatorname{id}_P)$ and use the total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The canonical $R$-linear chain map
$$a_P:C_r(P)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P\otimes_R S),\qquad a_P^q(y,x)=y\otimes1,$$
is a quasi-isomorphism, and for every chain map $h:P\to P'$ between K-flat complexes,
$$(h\otimes1)a_P=a_{P'}C_r(h),\qquad C_r(h)^q(y,x)=(h^q y,h^{q+1}x).$$
Both $C_r$ and $P\mapsto\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P\otimes_R S)$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Their localized functors on $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ are related by a natural isomorphism
$$A:C_r^D\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi L\varphi^*,$$
whose component at $Q_RP$, under the canonical K-flat computation of $L\varphi^*$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], is $Q_R(a_P)$. Write $i_P:P\to C_r(P)$ for $y\mapsto(y,0)$ and $\rho_P:P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P\otimes_R S)$ for $y\mapsto y\otimes1$. Then $a_Pi_P=\rho_P$, and after localization $A\circ i^D=\rho^D$, where $\rho^D$ is the derived scalar-extension unit. These comparisons agree under the canonical comparison between any two K-flat resolutions, satisfy the cocycle for three resolutions, and are natural for all derived morphisms.

proof.text: Write $B=C(r:R[0]\to R[0])$, so $B^{-1}=R$, $B^0=R$ and $d_B^{-1}=r$. The assumed short exact sequence, placed in degree zero, and [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] give a quasi-isomorphism $b:B\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi S[0]$ which is $\varphi$ in degree zero and zero in degree $-1$. This uses exactness as module sheaves, not surjectivity on all sections. In particular it applies on a site without points.

proof.text: For any complex $P$, tensor the cone defining $B$ on the right with $P$. The right-tensor cone comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs], followed by $R\otimes_RP\cong P$, identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(B\otimes_RP)$ with $C_r(P)$. Explicitly the $B^0\otimes P^q$ component is $y$ and the $B^{-1}\otimes P^{q+1}$ component is $x$; the total differential is $(dy+rx,-dx)$. The tensor unit maps are $a\otimes p\mapsto ap$, with inverse $p\mapsto1\otimes p$. In $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi S[0]\otimes_RP)$ the same cited tensor symmetry has sign $1$, giving the isomorphism to $T(P)=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(P\otimes_RS)$ by $s\otimes p\mapsto p\otimes s$. Therefore $b\otimes1_P$ is exactly $a_P(y,x)=y\otimes1$ in these coordinates. If $P$ is K-flat, the arbitrary-endpoint quasi-isomorphism assertion of the cited tensor lemma makes $b\otimes1_P$, and hence $a_P$, a quasi-isomorphism. No termwise flatness of $P$ or flatness of $S$ is used.

proof.text: The formula for $a_P$ is balanced and $R$-linear. It is a chain map since $a_Pd(y,x)=(dy+rx)\otimes1=dy\otimes1=d\,a_P(y,x)$, using $rx\otimes1=x\otimes\varphi(r)=0$. For an $R$-linear chain map $h$, $hr=rh$, so the displayed diagonal formula defines $C_r(h)$. Both composites in $T(h)a_P=a_{P\prime}C_r(h)$ send $(y,x)$ to $h(y)\otimes1$. Both $a_Pi_P$ and $\rho_P$ send $y$ to $y\otimes1$. These are identities of balanced presheaf tensor maps and therefore of their sheafifications; they hold for all complexes.

source.place: Principal quotient formulas; total tensor convention of Tag 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact).

proof.text: The complex $B$ is K-flat. Indeed for any acyclic $E$, the left-tensor cone comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs] identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(E\otimes_RB)$ with $C_r(E)$ (the shifted summand has sign $(-1)^p$ in degree $p$ of $E$). The map $r:E\to E$ is a quasi-isomorphism because its cohomology maps are the unique maps $0\to0$. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] its cone is acyclic; this is exactly the K-flat criterion [def-pc-kflat-complex] for $B$. Consequently tensoring on the right with $B$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism by the cited tensor lemma. The same cone comparison identifies this functor naturally with $C_r$, so $C_r$ preserves every quasi-isomorphism, including those between K-flat complexes. The tensor homotopy assertion also shows that $C_r$ induces a functor on $K(R)$.

By clause (1) of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], termwise scalar extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Exact restriction of scalars, as asserted in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], preserves cohomology and therefore quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $T$ preserves the required quasi-isomorphisms. Being additive and termwise, scalar extension and restriction also preserve cochain homotopies: applying them to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives the same equation. Hence $T$ is defined on the K-flat part of $K(R)$.

proof.text: First localize $QC_r$ on all complexes using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] and Step 4; call the resulting functor $C_r^D$. Let $\mathcal P_R\subset K(R)$ be the K-flat complexes with flat terms. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\to D(R)$ is an equivalence. On $\mathcal P_R$, $Q(a_P)$ is a natural isomorphism from $QC_r$ to $QT$ by Steps 2 and 3. Apply the natural-transformation clause of the localization universal property on $\mathcal P_R$ and transport across this equivalence. This gives a natural isomorphism $A:C_r^D\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi L\varphi^*$: the identification of the second functor is the canonical K-flat computation in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The cone comparison respects homotopies by Step 4 and $T$ does so by Step 5; thus this localization uses actual functors on the homotopy category, as required by the cited equivalence. The descended transformation is natural for every morphism of $D(R)$, not just localized chain maps.

proof.text:
It remains to verify the specified component on an arbitrary K-flat complex $P$, whose terms need not be flat. Choose $s:F\to P$ a K-flat resolution with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Let $c_P:\operatorname{Res}_\varphi L\varphi^*(Q_RP)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_RT(P)$ be the canonical computation isomorphism of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Its naturality gives $c_P(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi L\varphi^*)(Q_Rs)=Q_RT(s)c_F$. Naturality of $A$ and Step 3 now give
$$c_PA_{Q_RP}\,Q_RC_r(s)=Q_RT(s)c_FA_{Q_RF}=Q_RT(s)Q_R(a_F)=Q_R(a_P)Q_RC_r(s).$$
Cancel the invertible $Q_RC_r(s)$ (Step 4). Thus $c_PA_{Q_RP}=Q_R(a_P)$, with precisely the augmentation and precisely the canonical comparison requested.

proof.text: The inclusions $i_P$ are natural on all complexes and so descend to $i^D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. On flat-term K-flat $P$, [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], unit normalization (1), identifies the derived adjunction unit with $Q_R(\rho_P)$ under $c_P$. Step 3 therefore says $c_PA_{Q_RP}i^D_{Q_RP}=Q_R(a_P)Q_R(i_P)=Q_R(\rho_P)$. The equivalence $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\simeq D(R)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], together with the uniqueness clause for natural transformations under localization, extends this identity to all of $D(R)$. It is the asserted identity $A\circ i^D=\rho^D$ with the actual scalar-extension unit.

proof.text: For two K-flat resolutions $s:P\to X$ and $t:P\prime\to X$, set $v=(Q_Rt)^{-1}Q_Rs$. Naturality already proved on $D(R)$ says $A_{Q_RP\prime}C_r^D(v)=(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi L\varphi^*)(v)A_{Q_RP}$. In the computation coordinates of Step 7 this is exactly agreement under the canonical resolution comparisons. For a third resolution $u:P\prime\prime\to X$, the equation $((Q_Ru)^{-1}Q_Rt)((Q_Rt)^{-1}Q_Rs)=(Q_Ru)^{-1}Q_Rs$ proves the cocycle after applying either functor. The same naturality equation for arbitrary $v$ gives the last clause. No comparison chain map between two chosen resolutions is assumed.
